policy: Only validated complete measurement results whose complete benchmark input fingerprint matches may be reused. Eligible units are certified independently after their own validator passes, so a partial run can preserve completed work. Primary configuration is evaluation-scoped: an evaluation sees and hashes shared Primary policy plus only its own evaluation-local section, so changing Proficiency does not re-key Learnability, Language Quality, Semantic Compression, or Ecosystem. Units that measure Quidra are cacheable too: their historical key still carries the declared versions and exact Task Packet, while a separate trusted execution-identity check covers the actual compiler/runtime inputs. This preserves already-paid records without allowing same-version implementation changes to reuse stale results. Cache material is trusted runner input and is never exposed as a worker read path. The three Language Quality mechanical units (the micro suite, the adversarial set and the audit of the snapshot's Quidra programs) are certified too: no model is involved, so their key carries the pinned toolchains of every language they measure, the programs and fixtures they read, the measurement scripts, the snapshot's Quidra versions and a declared mechanical epoch; the raw samples stay in the run's retained artifact. Compatibility migrations are provenance-bearing: a recertified current record names and hashes its preserved source, records the migration rule/reason and transformed fields, and is rejected if that source provenance later fails integrity.
non_dependency_note: run_id, workflow identity, branch name, and host paths must never invalidate paid scientific evidence by themselves. Work-unit identity is currently part of the exact cache contract because the rendered Task Packet and validator ownership are unit-scoped; renaming/repartitioning a leaf therefore requires an explicit compatibility migration rather than silent reuse. Exact prompt/task content, assigned requirements, readable input hashes, model identity, toolchain identity, validators and declared epochs remain dependencies.

reuse_conditions.scored_output_cap: The output cap of a scored trial is not part of the key. A certified llm_learnability or llm_proficiency record carries what its trials did against the cap they ran under (scored_output_cap, trial_calls, cap_truncated_trial_calls, max_trial_output_tokens, written at promotion or by cache-annotate-caps from the run's retained agent traces). Under the same cap the record is reused. Under a different cap it is reused only when the cap demonstrably never mattered: no trial call was cut off and no completion was larger than the current cap. A record without this evidence is a MISS until it is annotated.
reuse_conditions.quidra_execution_identity: The historical fingerprint remains unchanged so already-paid cache stays addressable. Reuse of any record that measures Quidra additionally requires an exact compiler/runtime execution identity. New records carry it explicitly; legacy records are accepted only from verified migration commits while the target still equals the frozen migration baseline.
reuse_conditions.same_result_metadata_refresh: When reuse is rejected and a unit is freshly remeasured, identical result bytes do not preserve stale compatibility/certification metadata. The current trust metadata replaces the old record so changed Quidra execution identity or stronger certification cannot create a permanent MISS loop.
reuse_conditions.legacy_identity_ratchet: A verified legacy Quidra record that predates explicit execution identity may be rewritten at checkpoint with the current proven-equivalent execution identity while preserving its historical fingerprint and result. This is counted as an upgrade, not a remeasurement or replacement.
reuse_conditions.ecosystem_runner_rubric: Ecosystem cache reuse requires the same frozen runner-owned rubric. Historical language-local rubric scores are not recertified: retained paid records show that nominally identical metrics were actually scored with different rubrics across languages (for example four 25-point dimensions versus five 20-point dimensions), so reusing those scores would break cross-language comparability. Historical sources/findings remain preserved as evidence, but current scored cache requires the fixed rubric.
reuse_conditions.evaluation_scoped_primary_config: Primary Task Packets and cache keys include shared Primary policy plus only the current evaluation's local section. Methodology dependencies are likewise scoped to the sections actually embedded in that unit, and assigned-requirement metadata is hashed as the exact assigned projection rather than the whole catalog. Historical records created before these scoping migrations may be reused only when every unscoped prompt component and every other fingerprint dependency match exactly, the historical full Primary JSON projects to the same evaluation-specific configuration, and the historical selected methodology/assigned-requirement bodies are byte-identical to the current ones. A compatible hit is revalidated by the current validator and ratcheted to the current scoped fingerprint at checkpoint; disagreeing compatible records are not reused.

adversarial_language_shard_migration.reason: Explicit one-time migration of the certified all-language adversarial record to comparison-language shards. Reuse requires unchanged benchmark metadata, full LQ spec, frozen assets, complete reusable program tree, selected toolchain/runtime pins, epoch and requirement set. Quidra is excluded because the legacy key omitted snapshot-owned Quidra adversarial fixture hashes.

semantic_compression.reason: Automatic no-provider recertification for historical language-scoped Semantic Compression measurements. Model/provider, frozen sampling, toolchains, requirement set, Primary projection, evaluation specification and every non-SC readable input must still match exactly. Only the Task Packet hash, retired legacy validator-contract field, declared SC epoch, SC methodology-asset tree hash, and the later-added trusted F20 runtime-facts input may differ. F20.P1 is then re-adjudicated from those current trusted runtime facts before the current validator can approve the record. For downstream canonical-fragment consumers, the newly generated catalog path is projected out of the legacy fingerprint comparison only after the migration bridge proves that every non-NONE fragment actually recorded by the historical result is complete and byte-identical to the current canonical catalog; it then adds the current catalog attestation. The historical result is still staged under the current task and must pass the full current validator. Capability-coverage owners may be reconstructed only from preserved paid owner support plus fragment evidence from the same scientific experiment identity (same-run preferred; a different retained run is accepted only when provider, model, sampling, toolchains, benchmark metadata, Primary projection, SC methodology/spec, probe universe and every other shared dependency match exactly) and then re-adjudicated under the current rubric; consumers may bind raw-count-only shards to that catalog only under the same exact experiment-identity proof, while explicit legacy fragments must still match byte-for-byte. Any record that cannot satisfy those current checks remains a normal miss. LLM Proficiency is intentionally excluded because its prompt and repair trajectory are the scored experiment.

ecosystem_snapshot_recertification.reason: A trusted one-time snapshot centrally re-adjudicates preserved paid Ecosystem evidence under the frozen runner-owned v2 rubric. Hydration synthesizes only the current evidence shape and still runs the ordinary current validator before accepting a hit. The old language-local normalized score is never copied. Quidra additionally requires exact frozen compiler/runtime execution identity; if it changes, only Quidra falls back to fresh evidence collection.

llm_proficiency_trial_recertification.policy: Do not bridge Proficiency by epoch or unit result. Inspect preserved trials individually. A trial is only a recertification candidate when its exact current frozen trial ID, initial prompt bytes, model/provider/sampling identity and relevant toolchain identity all match, and no hidden-oracle evidence was model-visible during repair. Candidate trials still require deterministic replay through the current trusted verifier and current validator before they may contribute to a current-fingerprint certified record. Any mismatch is category E and must be rerun.
llm_proficiency_trial_recertification.current_legacy_audit: The 2026-09 historical Proficiency cache is intentionally not record-level migrated. The retained trial traces are audited separately by scripts/audit_proficiency_legacy.py; the current historical trials use a different scored task/prompt allocation, so they are not silently accepted merely because the old unit validator passed.

declared_epochs.note: Set by a person, like a toolchain pin. Ecosystem measures external packages, tools and public knowledge, which change independently of language versions. The runner-rubric-v2 epoch deliberately invalidates older Ecosystem score records because they were produced by language-local rubrics; the old records remain preserved in Git but are not score-compatible with the frozen runner-owned rubric contract.
declared_epochs.mechanical_note: Mechanical measurements are timed on the hosted runner class the workflow names. Change this value when that class changes or when the numbers should be taken again for another reason; nothing else about the runner enters the key.
declared_epochs.semantic_compression_note: Semantic Compression v6 preserves the mechanically verified canonical-fragment, trusted-runtime, machine-enforced R9, comparability-certified and fixed-stdout contracts. Historical language-scoped records are not blindly accepted across this epoch. When every scientific dependency except the SC methodology-asset tree, Task Packet serialization/hash and declared epoch still matches, the runner may stage the old result and run the full current validator. Only a current-validator PASS becomes a compatibility hit and is ratcheted to the v6 fingerprint; a rejection reruns only that leaf.
declared_epochs.llm_proficiency_note: LLM Proficiency v6 preserves the exact complete Primary trial allocation, prompt variants, trusted runtime verification and hidden-input correctness scoring, with hidden cases strictly score-only. There is no record-level epoch shortcut. Historical records remain preserved and are audited trial-by-trial: only an exact current-contract trial with no model-visible hidden feedback may advance to current mechanical re-verification; all others remain paid rerun candidates.

promotion.paid_partial_store: Private content-addressed Actions artifact (quidra-benchmark-paid-state) with Actions cache as a speed mirror; exact-fingerprint import only; hidden prompts/trials are never committed to public Git.

prompt_store.checkpoint_scope: Only prompt manifests/components referenced by cache records successfully certified in that checkpoint; raw provider responses/trials remain private paid-state artifacts.

quidra_execution_identity.purpose: Prevent stale same-version Quidra cache reuse without making benchmark-only commits cold. init records these Git object IDs before .git is excluded from the scored snapshot. New Quidra cache records certify that identity outside the historical fingerprint so existing valid records keep their paths.
quidra_execution_identity.legacy_note: Only legacy records from the listed source commits may use the baseline. Their Quidra execution inputs were verified to equal this map. 56f2c65 is intentionally excluded because its compiler/runtime inputs differ. Once the current target changes, every identity-less legacy Quidra record becomes a MISS even if project.toml keeps the same version.
